requirement: An mdBook chapter MAY contain one standalone `{requirements-index}` directive with an empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. A book MUST contain no more than one such directive. `habeas mdbook` MUST render a requirements index listing all requirements defined in rendered chapters, each linking to its evidence detail page under {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages`. When a directive is present, it MUST replace the directive with the index table; otherwise, it MUST generate the chapter specified by {cite}`requirements.index.chapter.default`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately cover `requirements.index.chapter`. I did not request implementation source; I judged the supplied test text against the requirement.

**Marker syntax (standalone directive, empty body, opening and closing colons)**
- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[marker_accepts_long_fences_and_ignores_examples]` checks that a four-colon marker is accepted and that a closing fence longer than the opening one (`::::` opened, `:::::` closed) is accepted.
- The same test rejects a marker with no closing fence, a marker with a non-empty body, and a closing fence shorter than the opening one.
- It ignores a marker inside a code fence, a marker nested inside another directive such as `{req}`, a two-colon marker, and an inline "Inline :::{requirements-index}" marker.
- It asserts the exact byte range replaced.

**At most one directive per book (MUST)**
- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[repeated_index_markers_fail_with_a_clear_error]` covers two markers in separate chapters and two markers in one chapter. Both cases assert that `preprocess_book` returns an error containing "only one".

**Index lists all requirements, each linking to its detail page**
- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]` places an explicit marker in an index chapter and asserts the following:
  - The marker text is gone from the index content.
  - Each of five requirements has a table row linking to `requirements-index/requirements.core.<name>.html`.
  - The row's state column is correct for each of the five states.
  - The table columns are aligned.
  - The index has six sub-items: five detail pages plus the coverage-gaps page.
- The same test checks detail-page paths, titles, section numbers and the back link to the index.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_owns_details_in_book_order_with_badge_icons]` checks that an explicit index keeps its placement, with detail pages in book order across chapters, including an example (`more.cli.mdbook`). It also checks that definitions link to the detail pages with the correct relative paths.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` checks that definitions in nested sub-chapters are included, that both requirements and examples are indexed, and that pages appear in definition order.

**Directive present replaces the directive; otherwise the default chapter is generated**
- Replacement is asserted in `index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters`.
- The no-marker default is asserted in `definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages` and `default_index_exists_even_without_definitions_or_numbered_chapters`.
- Together they cover:
  - the title "Requirements index" and the path `requirements-index.md`;
  - appending as a top-level chapter, with no source file and no parent names;
  - section number 1 when no chapter is numbered, and 3 after a chapter numbered 2;
  - the chapter existing with no definitions;
  - a marker inside a code block in prose not counting as a marker.
- The detailed behavior of `requirements.index.chapter.default` is a cited requirement. It is context only, and these tests also exercise it.

I found no unexercised obligation, and the assertions enforce the expected outcomes. No gaps and no acknowledgments.

text: An mdBook chapter MAY contain one standalone `{requirements-index}` directive with an empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. A book MUST contain no more than one such directive. `habeas mdbook` MUST render a requirements index listing all requirements defined in rendered chapters, each linking to its evidence detail page under {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages`. When a directive is present, it MUST replace the directive with the index table; otherwise, it MUST generate the chapter specified by {cite}`requirements.index.chapter.default`.
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate one evidence detail
page for every requirement and named example defined in a rendered chapter.
Each page MUST be a subchapter of the index chapter, in definition order,
titled by the definition's full name, at a path derived from the index chapter's
Books configured by {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` fold these subchapters in the
sidebar until a reader expands the index chapter.

When a book contains no standalone `{requirements-index}` directive, `habeas mdbook` MUST append a new top-level chapter titled "Requirements index" at `requirements-index.md`, containing the index table, even when the book defines no requirements or examples. The generated chapter MUST have no source file or edit target. Its section number MUST be one greater than the largest numbered top-level chapter, or 1 when no top-level chapter is numbered.
